info.name: Handpoint Cloud API
info.description:
# Handpoint Cloud API — Integration Collection

Complete request set for the Handpoint Cloud REST API. Covers card-present transactions, back-office operations, MOTO, and reporting.

## Quick start

1. **Import an environment** — use `Handpoint_Staging.postman_environment.json` (`.io`, no real funds) or `Handpoint_Production.postman_environment.json` (`.com`, live or DEMO merchant).
2. **Set your credentials** — fill `api_key`, `serial_number`, `terminal_type`, and `currency` in the active environment.
3. **Run `List Devices`** — confirms your API key is valid and shows assigned terminals.
4. **Run `Sale — Polling`** — sends a transaction to the terminal. The `TXN_RESULT_ID` variable is auto-populated from the 202 response. Run `Poll Result` until `finStatus` resolves.

## Variable chaining

Requests that produce a result automatically set collection variables for downstream requests:

| Set by | Variable | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Sale, Refund, Pre-Auth | `TXN_RESULT_ID` | Poll Result |
| Poll Result | `GUID` (`transactionID`) | Tip Adjustment, Reversal, Tokenize, Pre-Auth steps |
| Poll Result | `TXN_REF_ID` (echoed) | Status by Reference |
| Sale and Tokenize, Poll Result | `CARD_TOKEN` | MOTO Sale Back-Office |

## Amount units — critical inconsistency

| Endpoint | Amount format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /transactions` (all card-present) | **Minor units** as integer string | `"1000"` = €10.00 |
| `POST /moto/sale`, `/moto/refund`, `/moto/reversal` | **Major units** as decimal string | `"10.00"` = €10.00 |
| `POST /preauthorization/capture` — `capturedAmount` | **Major units** as decimal string | `"10.00"` = €10.00 |
| `POST /preauthorization/increase` — `increaseAmount` | **Major units** as decimal string | `"5.00"` = €5.00 |
| `POST /transactions/{id}/tip-adjustment` — `amount` | **Major units** as number | `5` = $5.00 |

## Docs

https://developer.handpoint.com

item.description: Verify credentials and discover assigned terminals.

request.description:
Returns all PAX terminals assigned to this merchant API key.

Run this first to confirm your credentials and discover `serial_number` and `terminal_type` values to use in transaction requests — both fields are required in `POST /transactions` and must exactly match what this endpoint returns.

- HTTP 200 = valid key
- HTTP 403 = wrong or missing `ApiKeyCloud` header
- Terminal absent from list = error `1004` on transaction requests

item.name: Card-Present Transactions
item.description:
All card-present operations route through `POST /transactions`. The terminal handles card reading, P2PE encryption, and cardholder interaction — your server never sees raw card data.

**Amount:** always **minor currency units** as an integer string. `"1000"` = €10.00 / $10.00.

**transactionReference:** UUID v4 — unique per original sale/refund/pre-auth. Do NOT include on subsequent operations (reversals, linked refunds, pre-auth captures). The server validates UUID v4 format — any other format returns HTTP 400.

**MOTO on-terminal:** keyed card entry on the PAX terminal (operator types card details). Uses the same endpoint and polling flow as a regular sale.

**Pre-Authorization:** the Create step is card-present; all subsequent lifecycle steps (Increase/Decrease, Capture, Reversal) are back-office and require no terminal.

exec: // Generate a fresh UUID v4 for transactionReference.
//   - position 17 (variant) must be 8, 9, a, or b
// transactionReference is used for GET /status recovery — persist it to your DB before sending.

body.raw:
{
  "operation": "sale",
  "amount": "1000",             // minor units — 1000 = 10.00 | ISO 4217 exponent 2 for EUR/USD/GBP/CAD
  "currency": "{{currency}}",   // ISO 4217 three-letter code: EUR, USD, GBP, CAD... — wrong value returns Agreement not found
  "terminal_type": "{{terminal_type}}",  // from GET /devices — e.g. PAXA920, PAXA920PRO, PAXA3700
  "serial_number": "{{serial_number}}",   // from GET /devices — 8-10 digit serial printed on device label
  "transactionReference": "{{TXN_REF_ID}}" // UUID v4 — unique per original sale — persist BEFORE sending for recovery
}

request.description:
Initiates a card-present sale on the PAX terminal. The terminal prompts the cardholder to tap, insert, or swipe.

**Flow:** POST → immediate 202 Accepted → terminal processes → poll `GET /transaction-result/{TXN_RESULT_ID}` until `finStatus` resolves (HTTP 204 = still processing, 200 = result ready).

**Key fields:**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | string | ✅ | Always `"sale"` for a sale |
| `amount` | string | ✅ | **Minor units** as integer string. `"1000"` = €10.00. Do NOT include decimal points. |
| `currency` | string | ✅ | ISO 4217 three-letter code (EUR, USD, GBP, CAD…) |
| `terminal_type` | string | ✅ | Must match device model — see GET /initialize |
| `serial_number` | string | ✅ | 8–10 digit PAX serial number |
| `transactionReference` | string | Recommended | UUID v4 you generate. Persist to DB before sending. Used for `/status` recovery if callback is lost. Do not reuse on subsequent operations. |
| `callbackUrl` | string | Optional | If present, result is POSTed to this URL when complete. Omit to use polling instead. |
| `token` | string | Optional | Echoed as `AUTH-TOKEN` header in the callback delivery. Used to authenticate the incoming webhook. |
| `tipConfiguration` | object | Optional | Enables on-screen tip prompt. See Sale with Tip Configuration. |
| `customerReference` | string | Optional | Free-text merchant reference (order ID, ticket number). Stored on the transaction record. Max 64 chars. |

**Poll cadence:** Wait 3s after 202, then poll every 4s. Maximum transaction time (full card fallback chain) is ~6 minutes — do not give up before then.

**`merchantReceipt` / `customerReceipt`:** returns a URL (`https://receipts.handpoint.io/...`) when the receipt was successfully uploaded to cloud storage, or raw HTML if the upload failed. Integrators must handle both formats.

request.description:
Sale with callback delivery. Handpoint POSTs the `TransactionResult` to your `callbackUrl` when the transaction completes — no polling needed.

**Additional fields vs. polling:**

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `callbackUrl` | string | HTTPS URL your server listens on. Must use a CA-signed TLS cert (Android 5–10 compatible — Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, etc.). Self-signed certs will silently fail. |
| `token` | string | Arbitrary string echoed as the `AUTH-TOKEN` header in the callback POST. Use to authenticate incoming webhooks — verify this matches before processing the result. |

**Callback delivery:** Your server must respond `2xx` to acknowledge. Handpoint may retry on non-2xx. Make your handler idempotent — deduplicate on `transactionReference`.

**Fallback:** If the callback is not received (network outage, server restart), recover via `GET /transaction-result/{TXN_RESULT_ID}` or `GET /transactions/{TXN_REF_ID}/status`.

**`merchantReceipt` / `customerReceipt`:** returns a URL (`https://receipts.handpoint.io/...`) when the receipt was successfully uploaded to cloud storage, or raw HTML if the upload failed. Integrators must handle both formats.

request.description:
Sale with an on-screen tip prompt shown to the cardholder on the PAX terminal after the sale amount is displayed.

**`tipConfiguration` fields:**

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `baseAmount` | string | Sale amount in **minor units** (same as `amount`). Used to compute percentage tip amounts shown on screen. |
| `headerName` | string | Text shown above the tip options on the terminal screen. |
| `tipPercentages` | integer[] | Up to 4 percentage values shown as quick-select buttons (e.g. `[10, 15, 20]` → 10%, 15%, 20%). |
| `enterAmountEnabled` | boolean | `true` = show a manual entry option for custom tip amount. |
| `skipEnabled` | boolean | `true` = show a "No Tip" / Skip button. |
| `footer` | string | Text shown at the bottom of the tip screen. |

**Result:** `tipAmount` in the `TransactionResult` reflects what the cardholder selected. `totalAmount` = `amount` + `tipAmount`.

**Note:** This shows a tip screen on the terminal at transaction time. This is different from post-sale tip adjustment (`POST /transactions/{id}/tip-adjustment`), which is an EPI-only back-office operation after the sale completes.

request.description:
Routes a card-present sale to a specific sub-MID using `merchantAuth`.

**`merchantAuth`** — pass an array with a single object containing `externalId`. The value must exactly match a sub-MID configured for the merchant in TMS. Omit `merchantAuth` entirely to route to the primary MID.

**Important:** The `externalId` is **not** echoed in the transaction result. Store it alongside the `transactionID` in your own system at request time.

**Invalid `externalId`** returns `finStatus: DECLINED` with `statusMessage: 'Invalid Merchant'` (`arc: '1000'`). The card must be fully presented before the decline is returned — this is a standard 202 + poll flow, not a 4xx error.

See [Multi-MID guide](/reference/multi-mid) for full routing rules and reconciliation guidance.

request.description:
Processes a sale flagged as a money transfer (MCC 4829 / MCC 6540). Adds Mastercard MoneySend fields to the transaction for remittance network routing.

**`moneyRemittanceOptions.fullName`:** recipient's full name, max 30 characters.

**`moneyRemittanceOptions.countryCode`:** ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (e.g. `"USA"`, `"GBR"`, `"MEX"`, `"DEU"`).

**Supported operations:** Sale, Sale & Tokenize, Refund, Linked Refund — same endpoint (`POST /transactions`) with `moneyRemittanceOptions` added.

**Acquirer:** EmerchantPay only. Verify support with your acquirer before enabling.

**Flow:** identical to a standard sale — 202 Accepted → poll `transaction-result/{TXN_RESULT_ID}` until `finStatus` resolves.

request.description:
Triggers a manual card-entry screen on the PAX terminal. The operator reads card number, expiry, and CVV from the cardholder and types them on the terminal. Supported by EPI, EmerchantPay, and Paystrax.

**Amount:** minor units as integer string — `"1000"` = €10.00.

**⚠ Known bug (CUS-837):** The `transactionReference` you send is NOT echoed back in the result. The result contains a system-generated reference. Recovery via `GET /{txnRef}/status` will not work. **Use `transactionResultId` (from the 202 response) to poll for the result.**

**Timeout:** If no operator enters card details, the poll loop exhausts (~120s → UNDEFINED). The terminal remains stuck in the active card-entry screen. Follow-up with `stopCurrentTransaction` to free it.

**Result:** `cardEntryType: "CNP"` confirms keyed entry. Receipts are delivered as raw HTML strings (not URLs) — handle both formats.

item.name: Keyed Entry Refund — Linked

request.description:
Card-not-present refund where the operator manually keys card details on the PAX terminal, linked to a previous transaction by its GUID.

**`originalTransactionId`:** the `transactionID` / `efttransactionID` from the original sale. Set from the `GUID` collection variable.

**Do not include `transactionReference`** — subsequent operations do not use it.

**Unlinked alternative:** omit `originalTransactionId` and include `transactionReference` — see **Keyed Entry Refund — Unlinked**.

**EMV alternative:** if the cardholder is physically present with their card, use **Refund — EMV Linked** (chip/tap, no manual key entry).

**Flow:** 202 Accepted → poll `transaction-result/{TXN_RESULT_ID}` until `finStatus` resolves. The terminal presents the card-detail entry screen — an operator must be present.

request.description:
Cancels the operation currently in progress on the terminal. Use after a polling timeout to free the terminal for the next transaction.

**When to use:**
- Your poll loop exhausted with `UNDEFINED` or no result and the terminal is stuck showing a processing screen
- An on-terminal MOTO (`moToSale`) timed out but no operator is present to cancel

**After sending:** poll this request's `TXN_RESULT_ID` until `finStatus: CANCELLED` before sending any new terminal request. Sending a new transaction while stop is in progress returns error `1001 Device is busy`.

**Response codes:**
- **202 Accepted** — stop request delivered to terminal. Poll `transaction-result/{transactionResultId}` to confirm the in-flight transaction was cancelled (the ongoing transaction's result arrives there).
- **400 error 1005** — no transaction is currently in progress on this terminal (immediate response, no polling).
- **400 error 1003** — cancel not allowed; the transaction is already being processed at the acquirer and cannot be interrupted.

item.description:
Hold-then-capture pattern for hospitality, car rental, and card-on-file scenarios.

**Pre-Authorization Create** is card-present — the cardholder presents their card at the PAX terminal and a hold is placed on their account. All subsequent lifecycle operations — Increase/Decrease, Capture, and Reversal — are back-office (no-reader) operations: no terminal or cardholder interaction is required, and Handpoint recommends using them server-side whenever possible.

**Supported acquirers:** EPI, EmerchantPay, Paystrax.

**Lifecycle:** Create → (optional) Increase/Decrease hold → Capture (charge) or Reversal (release hold without charge).

request.description:
Polls for the result of a `POST /transactions` request.

**`TXN_RESULT_ID`:** auto-populated from the 202 response. Format: `{serialNumber}-{unixTimestampMs}`. Do not construct this manually.

**Response codes:**
- `HTTP 204 No Content` — transaction is still processing. **Do NOT call `.json()` on this response — the body is empty and it will throw.** Wait 4s and poll again.
- `HTTP 200` — result is ready. Read `finStatus`.
- `HTTP 404` — ID not found or expired (older than 24h).

**`finStatus` values:**

| Value | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTHORISED` | Approved | Fulfil the order |
| `DECLINED` | Card declined | Show decline to operator; allow retry |
| `CANCELLED` | Cardholder cancelled | Allow retry |
| `PARTIALLY_AUTHORISED` | Partial amount approved | Collect remainder or reverse |
| `FAILED` | Terminal/network error | Log and investigate |
| `UNDEFINED` | No result received | Call GET /status; do NOT retry the transaction |

- `transactionID` (= `efttransactionID`) — use as `originalGuid` / `originalTransactionId` for all back-office operations
- `transactionReference` — your UUID v4, echoed back
- `totalAmount` — final charged amount (may differ from `requestedAmount` on partial approvals or when tip is added)
- `tipAmount` — tip selected by cardholder (0 if no tip)
- `cardToken` — populated only for `saleAndTokenizeCard`
- `cardSchemeName` — `Visa`, `Mastercard`, `American Express`, `Discover`, `Interac`
- `cardEntryType` — `CHIP`, `CHIPCONTACTLESS`, `SWIPE`, `CNP`
- `customerReceipt` / `merchantReceipt` — URLs to hosted receipt HTML pages (or raw HTML strings for on-terminal MOTO)
- `recoveredTransaction` — `true` if this result was returned by the SDK recovery mechanism

Queries the final status of a transaction by its `transactionReference`. Use this for UNDEFINED recovery when `transactionResultId` is lost (server crash, app restart, network drop).

**Base URL:** `transactions.handpoint.{{env}}` — note this differs from the Cloud API host (`cloud.handpoint.{{env}}`).

**`TXN_REF_ID`:** UUID v4 you generated for the original request. Must have been persisted to your DB before sending.

**Important — partial approval caveat:** This endpoint returns `AUTHORISED` as soon as the issuer responds, **before** the cardholder has accepted or declined the partial amount on the terminal. Do not use as your primary result poll. Use only after the `transactionResultId` polling loop exhausts or returns `UNDEFINED`.

**Status chain:** Add `/all` suffix to get the full operation chain (sale + refund + reversal) for a single `transactionReference`. Useful for pre-auth lifecycle tracking.

Also useful for get card token: if you need the original `SALE` transactionID after a partial approval → cancel flow, find the entry where `type == "SALE"` in the returned array.

item.description:
Server-side operations with no terminal or cardholder interaction required — all return synchronous HTTP 200/400 responses (no 202 / no polling), except Batch Close.

**Remote sale / refund / reversal (`/moto/*`):** charge a stored card token, refund it, or reverse it entirely. Amount in **major units** as a decimal string (`"10.00"` = €10.00) — different from the minor units used by `/transactions`.

**Get card token:** retrieve the card token generated by a `saleAndTokenizeCard` operation after the fact.

**Tip adjustment:** add a tip to a completed sale before the batch closes.

**Batch management (EPI only):** manually close the open batch and retrieve totals. Required once per business day for EPI merchants — missing a close causes ERR 005.

Adds a tip to a completed sale before the batch closes. EPI merchants only.

**`GUID`:** the `transactionID` from the sale result (the GUID variable in this collection).

**`amount`:** tip in **major currency units** as a number — NOT minor units. `5` = $5.00, `5.25` = $5.25. Do NOT send `500` expecting $5.00.

**Constraints:**
- Must be called before the day's batch closes (~11 PM EST for most EPI merchants)
- Not available on HiLite paths or Cordova

- `transactionID` must come from a SALE — not a reversal or pre-auth

**On failure after batch close:** HTTP 400 with error specific to acquirer.

request.description:
Charges a stored card token from your server — no terminal interaction, no cardholder present. EPI only.

**`amount`:** **major units** as a decimal string — `"10.00"` = €10.00. NOT minor units. Do NOT send `"1000"` expecting €10.00.

**`cardToken`:** obtained from a prior `saleAndTokenizeCard` or `GET /transactions/{id}/token`. Stored in the CARD_TOKEN collection variable.

**`transactionReference`:** UUID v4. Include for idempotency.

**Response:** HTTP 200 synchronous — no 202/polling. Check `httpStatus === 200` (integer field in body) for success. There is no `finStatus` field in this response.

**Reversal GUID:** the `guid` field in the response — NOT `transactionID`. Use in `POST /reversal` with `originalGuid`.

**Error `3107`:** Mandatory CVV is configured for this merchant's CNP — the token endpoint cannot supply CVV. Contact Handpoint to disable mandatory CVV.
**Error `5252`:** Token provider (ProCharge) is temporarily down — the token is valid, retry later.

**MOTO requirement:** Remote Sale uses the `/moto/sale` endpoint. **MOTO must be enabled for the merchant both in Handpoint and at the acquirer** before this endpoint will process successfully. Contact Handpoint support to enable MOTO.

Processes a linked refund without requiring the card or terminal to be present. Refunds against an original transaction identified by its GUID.

**Amount:** major units as a decimal string — `"10.00"` = €10.00. Different from the minor units used by `POST /transactions`.

**`originalGuid`:** the `guid` / `efttransactionID` from the original sale result (set the `GUID` collection variable from Poll Result).

**MOTO requirement:** Remote Refund uses the `/moto/refund` endpoint. **MOTO must be enabled for the merchant both in Handpoint and at the acquirer** before this endpoint will process successfully. Contact Handpoint support to enable MOTO.

**Card-present alternative:** use **Refund — EMV Linked** (Card-Present) when the cardholder is present at the terminal.

**Success:** HTTP 200 + `httpStatus: 200` + `issuerResponseCode: "00"`. No `finStatus`.

item.name: Device Commands
item.description:
Remote terminal management via the Cloud API. No cardholder interaction required.

**Requirements:**
- Handpoint Payments App **4.6.0+** on the terminal
- Terminal must be in **integrated mode** (configured via Handpoint TMS)

**`pingDevice`** routes through `POST /transactions` (same as a sale) and returns a 202 that can be polled for the connectivity result.

All other commands use `POST /devices/{terminal_type}/{serial_number}/{command}` and return `202 Accepted` immediately with no poll result. Command delivery is asynchronous — a `202` indicates the command was accepted, not that the terminal executed it.

item.name: Ping Device

request.description:
Confirms the terminal is reachable before sending a transaction, or after receiving error `1002` to check whether the device is back online. Lightweight — does not start a transaction or interact with the cardholder.

**When to use:**
- After a `1002` (No device listening) error, before retrying
- As a pre-flight health check in environments with unstable Wi-Fi

Do NOT use as a polling substitute — it creates unnecessary terminal traffic.

**Note:** `POST /reversal` goes directly to the payment host and is immune to terminal connectivity — a `pingDevice` check is never needed before a reversal.

**Flow:** 202 Accepted → poll `transaction-result/{TXN_RESULT_ID}`. A successful result confirms the device responded.

request.description:
Searches the transaction feed by time range and optional filters. Primary use case: UNDEFINED recovery when `transactionReference` recovery is unavailable.

**`startDate` / `endDate`:** format `yyyyMMddHHmmss` (e.g. `"20260905120000"`).

**`time_zone`:** IANA timezone string (e.g. `"Europe/London"`, `"America/New_York"`, `"UTC"`).

**`dummy`:** controls inclusion of test/simulator transactions:
- `"INCLUDE"` — include both real and dummy transactions
- `"ONLY"` — only dummy/simulator transactions
- `"NO"` — only real transactions

**Available `filters` fields:** `transactionReference`, `amount`, `maskedCardNumber`, `cardTypeId`, `approvalCode`, `terminalSerialNumber`

**UNDEFINED recovery pattern:** filter by `terminalSerialNumber` + narrow time window (±5 min around the original request). Match by `transactionReference` to identify the specific transaction — do NOT match by amount alone (multiple transactions may share the same amount).
